subject: Mutual action plan: acceptance criteria, API routes, and SDK routing
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@kommerce.ai>, Samir Shah <samir@kommerce.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan: acceptance criteria, API routes, and SDK routing

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Per our agreement on the call, I wanted to capture a concise mutual action plan (MAP) so both teams are clear on success criteria, the evaluation matrix, and the integration/ownership split for the trial. I attached a one‑page MAP (Kommerce_MAP_v1.xlsx) with the same content below.

High level recap and objectives
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Kommerce.ai's real‑time product recommendations pipeline (session scoring + personalization snippets).
- Scope for trial (2 weeks sandbox + 4 week pilot): API calls for generate/stream endpoints, SDK integration in Node service, and instrumented telemetry for quality checks.

Success criteria (primary acceptance gates)
1) Latency: p95 end‑to‑end <200ms for generate calls at 50 qps sustained
2) Throughput: sustained 50 req/s with autoscale to 150 burst
3) Quality: top‑3 recommendation accuracy >= 88% on Kommerce test set (we’ll provide eval harness)
4) Reliability: error rate <0.5% and graceful fallback to fallback‑model when capacity constrained
5) Observability: token‑level cost + per‑route latency traces available in Console for all trial traffic

Technical integration ask (initial):
- SDK: integrate redwood-node v0.9.2 (we've provided patch for advanced routing)
- API routes: use /v1/generate for batch scoring and /v1/stream for live snippets; function/tool calling will be used for product metadata enrichment via the toolcall route (/v1/toolcall)
- Streaming: prefer chunked server streaming for snippet render to avoid front‑end stalls; sample client code in attachment
- Authentication: token auth, rotate keys per sandbox owner (Kommerce to supply dev KMS key for Private pilot if needed)

Ownership and next steps
- Kommerce: supply sample dataset + eval harness (Priya) by Thu 7/22
- Redwood SE: Ben to produce SDK routing patch + sample streaming integration by Wed 7/21 (attached)
- Redwood Eng: Grace will validate throughput config and provide recommended autoscale policy by Fri 7/23
- Sales: I (Jordan) to coordinate kickoff, SOW checklist and carrier procurement if needed

Proposed timeline
- 7/21: delivery of SDK patch + sample code
- 7/22: Kommerce uploads eval dataset and test harness link
- 7/24: sandbox kickoff (2 weeks)
- 8/07: preliminary acceptance review

Please confirm or call out changes — if everyone agrees I’ll convert the MAP to a HubSpot mutual action plan record and send calendar invites for the sandbox kickoff.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Kommerce_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP), redwood-sdk-routing-0.9.2.patch (diff), kommerce-demo-telemetry-sample.json (example)
From: Ellen Park <ellen@kommerce.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@kommerce.ai>, Priya Nair <priya@kommerce.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: acceptance criteria, API routes, and SDK routing

Jordan — thanks for the detailed MAP. Confirming Kommerce can meet the following:
- We’ll upload a 10k sample eval set and the automated harness by 7/22 (Priya will own).
- Acceptance metric: we prefer a slightly higher accuracy floor (90%) for production readiness, but 88% is fine for pilot acceptance; we’ll document the pass/fail gating in the harness.

Technical clarifications:
- For streaming, we need explicit per‑chunk sequence ids to reassemble snippets on our side. Is the /v1/stream path able to include sequence headers?
- How does the fallback to a smaller quantized model affect tokenization and prompt shape? We want to avoid downstream truncation differences.

We’re good with the timeline in principle — please loop in your SEs for a quick pairing session on Wednesday 7/21. Also, can you provide a short list of telemetry fields Redwood will emit during the trial (trace id, tokens, cost, model_id, p95 latency)? That’ll help us wire our observability.

— Ellen
Head of Engineering
Kommerce.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@kommerce.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: acceptance criteria, API routes, and SDK routing

Ellen — quick answers and attachments below.

1) /v1/stream sequence support
We include a small JSON header for each chunk with sequence_id and chunk_index when using the chunked streaming protocol. Sample: {"sequence_id": "sess‑abc123", "index": 3, "final": false}. The sample client in redwood-sdk-routing-0.9.2.patch demonstrates reassembly.

2) Fallback model behavior
- Tokenization and prompt length are preserved across model variants; we maintain a compatibility shim that normalizes prompt shaping so truncation behavior matches the primary model. Small differences can still occur for edge tokens — we'll surface a mismatch score in telemetry (mismatch_pct).

3) Telemetry fields (trial exports)
We will emit: trace_id, request_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_cost_usd, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_code, fallback_used (bool), mismatch_pct. Sample telemetry JSON attached (kommerce-demo-telemetry-sample.json).

4) SDK routing patch
Attached is a small patch to redwood-node v0.9.2 that adds: route affinity header (x-rw-route), client side batching opt in (batchHint), and streaming chunk headers. Use the patch to validate on your sandbox environment; we can cut a release if you prefer.

Ownership and blockers
- Ben (SE): I’ll pair with Priya on 7/21 at 2pm PT to walk the SDK patch.
- Grace (Eng): Grace will validate autoscale parameters; if we need extra GPUs for pilot we’ll surface a Dedicated reserved plan estimate.

Next actions
- Priya (Kommerce) to confirm 7/21 2pm PT pairing and upload dataset by 7/22
- Jordan to create HubSpot MAP record and share kickoff invite after confirm

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
